Why Midlothian businesses miss calls

Midlothian sits on US-67 in Ellis County, where cement and steel have long been major industries. Manufacturing employs about 13% of workers, and median household income is about $127,000 as new neighborhoods fill in. Long-time local businesses now serve many newcomers who find them through a search and call straight away. A voicemail on that first call can lose a customer who has no reason to wait.

Which Midlothian businesses benefit most?

  • HVAC and contractors: New homes mean more calls than a small crew can answer.
  • Dental offices: New families need a regular dentist.
  • Auto repair shops: Plant workers need booking around shifts.

Can you keep your Midlothian phone number?

Yes. Midlothian callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
